issues.description: Right-side Bash popup - command text overflows popup width; CommandView flexWrap+flex:1 defeats outer horizontal ScrollView
issues.target_layer: L1 cosmetic / L2 structural (style flags on existing ScrollView)
issues.details: Horizontal ScrollView is declared but inner row uses flexWrap:'wrap' + child flex:1 which forces wrap-and-overflow instead of scroll. Dev must reproduce at popup width and pick: remove flexWrap, tighten container maxWidth/overflow, or constrain the flex:1 child so ScrollView owns scrolling.
issues.observation_notes: User spec 5.3. Applies all viewport widths (desktop/narrow/tablet/mobile). Related to 5.6 - fix applies to Codex popup once unified through shared primitives.
issues.ordering_rationale: Shared component CommandView is used by both Claude Code and (post-5.6) Codex popups. Fix here propagates to both flavors once 5.6 unifies them.

issues.details: updateSessionModelMode currently writes Zustand only, no MMKV. Mirror permission-mode plumbing (storage.ts:834-862, persistence.ts:191-206). Add 'session-model-modes' MMKV key. Add load-time MMKV override in modelMode resolution (storage.ts:320-339 equivalent). Add model chip to AgentInput footer immediately left of permission badge.

issues.ordering_rationale: Highest-certainty fix - exact mirror of existing permission-mode plumbing. Run early for a quick Tier-1 win.

issues.description: 1M-context Claude models - context-usage display broken (shows 0% left); MAX_CONTEXT_SIZE hardcoded to 190000
issues.target_layer: L4 logic (per-model lookup replaces hardcoded constant)
issues.details: MAX_CONTEXT_SIZE=190000 is the denominator for all models. For 1M-context sessions, contextSize > 190000 -> percentageUsed > 100 -> percentageRemaining clamps to 0. Fix: introduce getModelContextWindow(modelKey) co-located with modelModeOptions.ts (default 200k, 1M for [1m]/1M family), thread model identifier into getContextWarning, replace hardcode with resolved per-session maximum.
issues.observation_notes: User spec 5.2. Scope: every 1M Claude variant in the picker. Existing warning thresholds (<=5%, <=10%) are percentage-based and remain correct once denominator is right.
issues.ordering_rationale: Small, localized fix with clear acceptance test (open a 1M session, observe non-zero percent).

issues.description: Long background-task disconnect causes out-of-order delivery on reconnect; reconnect only happens when user sends next message
issues.location: happy transport/relay/delivery-queue layer (packages/happy-app/sources/sync/ and potentially packages/happy-server/sources/app/ or happy-cli transport)
issues.details: Failure sequence: long background task -> happy<->claude connection drops -> reconnect only triggered by next user message -> happy forwards Claude's background-task self-reply BEFORE the reply to the user's new message, even though Claude processes them in correct order. Root cause: happy's delivery queue / event re-ordering after reconnect. Fix requires: (1) proactive reconnect during long background tasks (not user-trigger-gated), (2) causal ordering guarantee in the delivery queue.
issues.observation_notes: User spec 5.10. Not a UI bug - backend transport. No reference screenshot; sequencing bug.
issues.skip_reason: Large cross-package transport-layer fix requiring proactive reconnect + causal ordering queue changes. Too complex for remaining ~3.5h budget alongside 10+ UI fixes. Requires dedicated cycle with reproducible repro setup (long background task). Deferred to next session with priority.
issues.ordering_rationale: Large infrastructure change. Defer to a dedicated cycle.
issues.deferral_context: Non-negotiable user requirement deferred to next session. Transport-layer work warrants its own cycle with dedicated repro/monitoring infrastructure.

pm_notes.description: Run 5.17 + 5.16 + 5.8 as a grouped markdown-parser workstream - they share MarkdownView/parseMarkdown pipeline. A single parser activation fix may resolve multiple headings/strikethrough/lists/LaTeX issues simultaneously.
Run 5.18 before 5.6 - 5.18 establishes the 'compact inline card + verbose sidebar' pattern that 5.6 and the future 5.15 work must follow.
Run 5.6 + 5.3 together - 5.6 unifies Codex through CommandView, and 5.3 fixes CommandView's flexWrap overflow issue. Both flavors benefit from the combined fix.
5.1 and 5.2 are independent quick wins with clear specified file paths. Run after shared-primitive groups complete.
5.4 + 5.5 share a fix - pair them in the same pipeline. QA uses 5.5's scenario as a validation case for 5.4's fix.

DEFERRALS are to NEXT SESSION, not dropped. 5.10, 5.13, 5.14, 5.15 remain Tier 1 non-negotiable user-spec items. Next session's PM must open with them as the top of the priority stack. Per User-Spec Item Protection rules, severity stays Tier 1 in RETRO - no downgrade permitted.

5.15 should be phased across future cycles: cycle-next = Category A Web (10 tools), cycle-n+1 = Category B Local-exec (10 tools), cycle-n+2 = Categories C+D (7 tools). Each phase uses shared primitives established by 5.6 + 5.18 this cycle.

QA must verify ALL UI fixes on BOTH desktop (1280+) AND mobile (390x844) viewports per the 2026-04-04 E2E mandate. Dev environment session may not have live LaTeX / wide tables / Codex tools - QA must SEND MESSAGES in a live session to trigger the test content, not skip verification.

strategic_notes: Cycle planned as follows given ~3.5h budget: Pipelines 0-13 (14 pipelines, all Tier 1 user-spec items) ordered to maximize shared-primitive amortization. Parser group (5.17, 5.16, 5.8) runs first. Tool-rendering pattern (5.18) establishes pattern. Codex-popup group (5.6, 5.3) unifies primitives. Then isolated quick wins (5.1, 5.2, 5.11, 5.7, 5.9). Finally structural layout (5.4+5.5) and composer UX (5.12). Pipelines 14-17 (5.15, 5.13, 5.14, 5.10) DEFERRED to next session - 5.15 is genuinely 4-8h of work (25+ tool renderers), 5.10 is a cross-package transport/ordering fix. Deferrals are NOT drops - they remain Tier 1 and MUST lead the next session's priority stack per User-Spec Item Protection. Expect realistically 8-12 of the 14 non-deferred to ship; remaining carry forward.
